# A. Argentina {#arg}

Section {{< var p.sec_argentina >}} of the paper calibrates the model with informal households to Argentina before
its coverage reforms and reads the reforms as a rise of the universal pension ε; appendix {{< var p.app_EPH >}}
gives the household survey and the identification. This part shows how the equilibrium depends on the whole
pension design, how the reform and the calibration depend on the intertemporal elasticity of substitution (IES),
and what changes when the taste for leisure is identified quartile by quartile.

- [A1. How pension designs shape the equilibria](arg-designs.qmd): the equilibrium in 2010 over every design
  (ε, θ), with the reform as a move across it.
- [A2. The intertemporal elasticity of substitution](arg-ies.qmd): the calibration at every IES of the grid, and
  the reform's paths in levels at the IES you choose.
- [A3. Identification of X](arg-leisure.qmd): the paper's common taste for leisure against one per quartile.
